title: Transport of derived open units along a scheme isomorphism
statement: Let X be a scheme with chosen derived categories for module sheaves on X and all localized open sites [def-pc-derived-category]. Let A be a commutative ring, a:Spec(A)\simeq X a scheme isomorphism, and U an open of X. There exist chosen derived categories in the same morphism universe on Spec(A) and all its localized open sites, an equivalence F:D(O_Spec(A))\simeq D(O_X), right adjoints R_S,R_X to exact derived restriction to a^{-1}U and U, and adjunctions. The functor of F is identified, after precomposition with localization, with termwise restriction along a^{-1} followed by localization. F and its inverse preserve quasi-coherent homology; F preserves perfection [def-pc-perfect-complex]. For every Q, vanishing of its homology stalks on a^{-1}U implies vanishing of the homology stalks of F(Q) on U. The functor of F has a coherent structure commuting with integer shifts. For all K the adjunction unit on X is invertible if and only if the unit on Spec(A) at F^{-1}(K) is invertible. This is a transport statement for arbitrary objects, with no Koszul or orthogonality-detection conclusion.

proof.text: Restriction along a^{-1} and a gives mutually inverse exact equivalences on module sheaves. Their termwise action preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Transport the supplied chosen localizations through these equivalences, also for corresponding opens, retaining the same morphism universe. Localize to obtain F and its specified natural comparison with termwise restriction along a^{-1}. This identifies the functor up to natural isomorphism and is not a choice of an arbitrary derived object. The comparison of sections on corresponding opens identifies the two restriction functors.

Open restriction is exact. Its right adjoint is derived direct image computed on K-injective resolutions. Specialize the ringed-space derived adjunction to the open immersion and identify exact derived pullback with the localization of restriction, transported between the localized site and the open subscheme. Conjugate the resulting adjunction by the equivalences from step 1. The conjugated unit is the image of the original unit composed with invertible comparison morphisms. Equivalences reflect isomorphisms, so the two unit components are invertible simultaneously, for every K.

The exact equivalence from step 1 commutes with homology and shifts, and identifies stalks at corresponding points via the isomorphism of local rings. Thus it preserves quasi-coherence in both directions and transfers stalk vanishing on the corresponding opens. Transfer each strictly perfect local representative, its finite free terms and retractions, to obtain perfection. The termwise functors commute with integer cochain shifts, and their shift comparisons descend through localization with the zero and addition coherence identities. This supplies CommShift, from which the consuming proof derives the Hom equivalence using F.toAdjunction.homEquiv. Empty schemes and empty or full opens require no nonemptiness assumptions.

theorem affine_derived_open_transport
    (X : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ U : X.Opens, HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (a : Spec (.of A) ≅ X) (U : X.Opens) :
    ∃ hD : HasDerivedCategory.{w}
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (Spec (.of A)).toRingedSpace)),
    letI := hD
    ∃ hO : ∀ V : (Spec (.of A)).Opens, HasDerivedCategory.{w}
        (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings (Spec (.of A)).toRingedSpace).over V)),
    letI := hO
    ∃ (F : schemeDerivedCategory (Spec (.of A)) ≌ schemeDerivedCategory X)
      (RS : DerivedCategory
        (SheafOfModules.{u}
          ((moduleRings (Spec (.of A)).toRingedSpace).over (a.hom ⁻¹ᵁ U))) ⥤
        schemeDerivedCategory (Spec (.of A)))
      (RX : DerivedCategory
        (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U)) ⥤
        schemeDerivedCategory X)
      (adjS : (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
        (moduleRings (Spec (.of A)).toRingedSpace) (a.hom ⁻¹ᵁ U)).mapDerivedCategory ⊣ RS)
      (adjX : (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
        (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U).mapDerivedCategory ⊣ RX),
      Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ F.functor ≅
        (@Functor.mapHomologicalComplex ℤ
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (Spec (.of A)).toRingedSpace))
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) _ _ _ _
          (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor a.inv)
          ⟨fun M N ↦ (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor a.inv).map_zero M N⟩
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q) ∧
      (∀ Q, schemeDerivedQCohProperty (Spec (.of A)) Q →
        schemeDerivedQCohProperty X (F.functor.obj Q)) ∧
      (∀ K, schemeDerivedQCohProperty X K →
        schemeDerivedQCohProperty (Spec (.of A)) (F.inverse.obj K)) ∧
      (∀ Q, Scheme.IsPerfect (Spec (.of A)) Q →
        Scheme.IsPerfect X (F.functor.obj Q)) ∧
      (∀ Q, (∀ (n : ℤ) (x : Spec (.of A)), x ∈ a.hom ⁻¹ᵁ U →
        Subsingleton (↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (Spec (.of A)).toRingedSpace)) n).obj
            Q).val.presheaf x))) →
        ∀ (n : ℤ) (x : X), x ∈ U →
          Subsingleton (↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
            (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) n).obj
              (F.functor.obj Q)).val.presheaf x))) ∧
      Nonempty (F.functor.CommShift ℤ) ∧
      (∀ K, IsIso (adjS.unit.app (F.inverse.obj K)) ↔ IsIso (adjX.unit.app K))
